title: Silver Support income threshold and the Local Qualifying Salary
asked: Why the Silver Support Scheme's higher-tier monthly income per person threshold stays at $1,500 when the Local Qualifying Salary is $1,600, and whether the Ministry will review that threshold for consistency and adequacy of support for lower-income seniors.
response: Dr Tan See Leng said the $1,500 threshold refers to monthly per capita household income, not an individual's monthly income, and that payouts are tiered by flat type and PCHI. He said the Local Qualifying Salary serves a different purpose, ensuring firms employing foreign workers pay local workers meaningfully, and is not a measure of retirement adequacy or financial need. He said the Silver Support Scheme was enhanced in 2025, with the qualifying monthly PCHI threshold raised from $1,800 to $2,300, about a 28% increase, and that the scheme will continue to be reviewed periodically.

key_points.point: The $1,500 higher-tier threshold is a monthly per capita household income figure, not an individual's monthly income.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: the $1,500 threshold for the higher tier of payouts in the Silver Support Scheme refers to the monthly per capita household income (PCHI)

key_points.point: PCHI is total gross household monthly income divided by the number of family members living together.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: This monthly PCHI is computed as the total gross household monthly income, divided by the total number of family members living together in the same household.

key_points.point: Silver Support payouts are tiered by flat type as well as monthly PCHI.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: Our Silver Support Scheme payouts are tiered by flat types

key_points.point: The Local Qualifying Salary exists to make firms employing foreign workers pay local workers meaningfully rather than token salaries.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: It is to ensure that firms who wish to employ foreign workers also pay their local workers meaningfully, rather than on token salaries.

key_points.point: The Local Qualifying Salary is not intended as a measure of retirement adequacy or financial need.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: It is not intended as a measure of retirement adequacy or financial need

key_points.point: The Silver Support Scheme was enhanced in 2025, raising the qualifying monthly PCHI threshold from $1,800 to $2,300.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: we recently enhanced the Silver Support Scheme, just last year, in 2025, and we raised the qualifying monthly PCHI threshold from $1,800 to $2,300

key_points.point: The Ministry will keep reviewing the Silver Support Scheme periodically.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: we will continue to review the Silver Support Scheme periodically

key_points.point: There are further refinements to the Local Qualifying Salary coming in the upcoming Budget and Committee of Supply.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: There will be further refinements to the LQS in the upcoming Budget, the Committee of Supply.

key_points.point: The Minister said he does not have statistics on how many seniors were pushed below the $1,500 monthly PCHI threshold by LQS changes.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: I do not have those statistics because it is not how we work that scheme out to be

left_open: Any assessment of whether seniors whose wages were adjusted by employers to meet the Local Qualifying Salary were pushed into a lower Silver Support tier.
The number of Silver Support recipients who moved from the higher tier to a lower tier since the LQS increase to $1,600.
supplementary: Whether LQS increases push seniors living alone into lower Silver Support tiers, and how many recipients have moved tiers.
